diagnosis.summary: payment-service is the only affected service, with its request rate rising from 0.94 rps to 1.87 rps while p95 latency held nearly flat at 4.63 ms against a baseline of 4.51 ms. The 5xx error rate remains at 0. The classifier identifies this as a DATABASE_THROTTLING incident with very high confidence.
diagnosis.root_cause: Database throttling on a dependency upstream of payment-service is the most likely root cause, consistent with the near-doubling of request rate and stable latency tail that has not yet surfaced errors.
evidence: Request rate to payment-service rose from 0.94 rps to 1.87 rps, an increase of approximately 98%.
p95 latency moved only marginally, from 4.51 ms to 4.63 ms, a change of about 2.7%.
5xx error rate is 0 at both baseline and current, with no errors surfacing despite the elevated request rate.
recommended_actions: Check read_throttle_events and throttled_requests on the DynamoDB tables accessed along the call path that reaches payment-service, particularly on the Orders table, to confirm which table is throttling.
Review db_latency_ms_p95 on order-service to determine whether tail latency is rising there, since order-service calls payment-service on every POST /orders.
Monitor payment-service p95_latency_ms and error_rate_5xx over the next several minutes; if the request rate remains elevated, 5xx errors may appear as retries are exhausted.
After identifying the throttled table, raise its provisioned capacity or switch it to on-demand mode to relieve the throttle.
Recheck read_throttle_events and db_latency_ms_p95 on the affected table after each capacity change to confirm improvement.
